Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot order — termination / auto-renew questions

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — the Quantica infra team is excited to get the pilot started. Our procurement lead asked me to clarify a couple of contract items before we execute the order form:

1) Auto-renew: The order form currently has a 12-month term with automatic renewal unless we give 60 days' notice before renewal. For pilots, Procurement is pushing for the ability to opt out earlier (they suggested 30 days) because budget cycles are shorter.

2) Termination for convenience: They want to confirm whether Quantica can terminate the pilot without cause and whether there are any wind-down fees or data export assistance obligations.

Could you share your standard approach for pilot deals and whether Redwood can make exceptions for notice windows on short pilots? If you need to loop legal, we can be patient, but hope to close the commercial side this week.

Also attaching the signed order form draft for reference.

Thanks,
Evan

Thanks for flagging. Commercial view: we want to keep renewal cadence predictable for paid customers, but pilots should have more flexibility. Proposal to balance both sides:

- Order form term remains 12 months but for pilot-labeled orders we allow a 30-day opt-out before renewal (instead of the standard 60). This only applies to accounts tagged as "pilot" in our billing system.
- No wind-down or early exit fees for pilots; final invoice pro rata for days used in final month.
- We offer a 30-day data export window after effective termination; professional services for large exports charged separately and disclosed upfront.

If legal is comfortable with the pilot carve, I can accept on behalf of Sales. Laura — see attached suggested redline in MSA for a pilot exception.

Aditya

Subject: Re: Pilot order — termination / auto-renew questions

I've reviewed and added targeted redlines. Main items:

1) Auto-renew / notice window
Proposed text to insert into Order Form (short form):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Term and Renewal) of the MSA, for any Order Form designated as a 'Pilot' (as indicated in the Order Form), Customer may elect not to renew the Order Form by providing written notice to Redwood no later than thirty (30) days before the then-current Term's expiration date. All other MSA renewal mechanics remain in effect."

Rationale: narrowly scoped, one-sentence carve that preserves MSA mechanics but gives Quantica the 30-day pilot opt-out they requested. Keeps renewal economics consistent for non-pilot accounts.

2) Termination for convenience
Recommended MSA paragraph (redline):
"Either party may terminate an Order Form designated as a 'Pilot' for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Upon termination for convenience by Customer, Redwood will invoice Customer for Services provided through the effective date of termination on a pro rata basis. Redwood will provide Customer with access to Customer data for thirty (30) days following termination to permit orderly export; Redwood may, at its discretion, offer professional services to assist with exports, which will be charged at then-current rates."

Rationale: 30-day pilot termination is reasonable for short engagements and aligns with Aditya's commercial suggestion. For enterprise, we keep the standard 60-day notice in the MSA.

3) Clean fallback language
I added a short sentence confirming that nothing in the pilot carve modifies the MSA's limitation of liability or data handling provisions. Keeps scope controlled.

If Sales is happy, I'll prepare a tracked MSA + order form to send to Quantica. One ask: Aditya, confirm which field you want to use to flag pilot orders (I assume "order_type=pilot" in our billing meta).

Laura

Evan / Olivia — thanks for your patience. We've agreed internally on conservative, targeted edits so we don't change enterprise defaults but accommodate the pilot ask. Summary of the agreed language we're proposing (attached as tracked changes):

- Pilot opt-out: For Order Forms explicitly designated as a "Pilot," Customer may provide written notice to opt out of auto-renewal no later than 30 days before the expiration of the then-current term.
- Pilot termination for convenience: Customer may terminate a Pilot Order Form for convenience with 30 days' written notice. Redwood will invoice for services provided through the effective date (pro rata) and provide access to Customer data for 30 days after termination. Professional services for assisted exports are available and charged separately.
- No change to MSA liability / data handling; these remain as-is.

Next steps: Laura will attach a tracked MSA + updated Order Form. If Quantica is good with these edits we can route the two documents for signature via DocuSign and aim to start the pilot on Aug 1.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.net/sign/QNT-4521-order
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/QNT-4521
